text: The line graph shows the percentage of household waste that was recycled in Germany, Britain and Poland over a period of twenty years, from 2000 to 2020. The data covers five-year intervals.

Overall, the recycling rate went up in all three countries. Germany had the highest rate in every year, while Poland had the lowest rate throughout the period, although the gap between the countries became smaller.

In 2000, Germany recycled 48% of its household waste, and this figure rose steadily to 67% in 2020. The increase was fastest between 2000 and 2010, and after that the rate grew more slowly, with only a small rise of one percentage point in the last five years.

Britain and Poland started from much lower levels. Britain recycled only 11% of its waste in 2000, but this rose to 44% in 2020, which was a big change. Poland began at just 4% and increased to 35% by the end of the period. As a result, the difference between Germany and Poland fell from 44 percentage points to 32.
